title: The Dark Wolf Nebula
caption: The Dark Wolf Nebula, imaged by the VLT Survey Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Dark clouds form the silhouette of a wolf against a colourful backdrop of glowing gas. The resemblance has earned this cloud the nickname Dark Wolf Nebula. The shape is an illusion made by cold cosmic dust blocking the light from the glowing clouds behind it.

Dark nebulae like this are places where gas and dust are thick and cold enough to hide what lies beyond them. They are also where new stars are born: in their densest parts, material can collapse under gravity and eventually ignite. The nebula is catalogued as a star-forming region.

The image comes from the VLT Survey Telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile, a telescope designed to photograph large areas of sky in detail. It is a big picture, with 283 million pixels, which lets it capture both the broad outline of the wolf and fine detail in the surrounding glowing clouds.
scale: The nebula is around 5300 light-years from Earth, according to ESO.

understand.summary: The VLT Survey Telescope's OmegaCAM camera made this visible-light image through u, g, r and i filters plus a hydrogen-alpha filter; the colour mapping isn't published.
filters: 354 nm · Optical u (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
475 nm · Optical g (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
625 nm · Optical r (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
659 nm · Optical H-alpha (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
756 nm · Optical i (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
understand.eye: The camera builds up faint glowing gas over long exposures, so the colourful backdrop would be far dimmer to the eye.
